learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to utilize unused roof space to grow plants, fresh vegetables, and contribute to a greener, cooler urban environment!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is the practice of cultivating gardens on the roof of a building. It is a fantastic way for city dwellers (urban areas) to grow their own food where land is scarce.
It provides fresh organic vegetables, reduces the temperature of the building (natural cooling), cleans the air, and looks beautiful!
Since roofs cannot handle too much heavy wet mud, lightweight soil mixes (like coco peat, perlite, and compost) are used in plastic or grow-bag containers.
Before starting, the roof MUST be waterproofed to prevent leaks into the house. Containers must have holes at the bottom so excess water can drain out.
Roofs get direct, harsh sunlight. Choose plants that love the sun (like tomatoes, chilies, and brinjals) and set up green shade nets to protect delicate plants.

fun_activity.title: 🪴 The Cup Garden
fun_activity.instructions: Take an empty yogurt cup and poke a small hole in the bottom. Fill it with soil, plant a few coriander (dhaniya) seeds, and water it lightly. Keep it on your windowsill or roof and watch your mini garden grow!

exam_tips: 📌 Always mention 'waterproofing' as the most critical first step in rooftop gardening.
📌 Explain why regular garden soil is not ideal for roofs (it becomes too heavy when wet).
📌 List 3 benefits of rooftop gardening for urban environments (cooling, fresh air, aesthetics).
quick_recap: ⭐ Rooftop gardens help reduce the 'Urban Heat Island' effect in concrete cities.
⭐ Drip irrigation is highly recommended for rooftops to prevent water wastage.
⭐ Start small with herbs (mint, coriander) before moving to heavy fruiting vegetables.
